_comment: The trust policy for a Confidential sample's dedicated EKS Pod Identity role. A
sample's setup script drops this _comment key, fills in the placeholders and passes
<CLUSTER_NAME>     the cluster the pod runs on
The three aws:RequestTag conditions are what scope the role to one service account on
one cluster: EKS Pod Identity sets them as session tags when it assumes the role, so
without them any Pod Identity association in the account could assume it. sts:TagSession
is required alongside sts:AssumeRole because the service passes those tags.
Source: EKS Pod Identity and its role trust policy in the Amazon EKS User Guide,
'Grant pods access to AWS resources with EKS Pod Identity'.
The role gets no identity policy, attached or inline. Everything it may do lives in
the KMS key policy next to this file, where the attestation condition sits, so there
is no second path to kms:Decrypt that skips the gate. A sample's setup script checks
that the role has no identity policies and stops if it finds one.
